question.worked_solution:
We start by changing the variable:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =2x-1 \\ \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =2 \\ \text{d}u & =2\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u & =\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we create a table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=2x-1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 1 & 2 \\ u & 1 & 3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
{\int }_{1}^{2}\sqrt{2x-1}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1}^{3}\sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we can solve it and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}\sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\cdot \frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2}|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}({3}^{3/2}-{1}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(({3}^{3})^{1/2}-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(3\sqrt{3}-1) \\  & =\sqrt{3}-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
